source.check: returned unopposed: the News-Letter's nominations report states there were 'only three changes in the personnel of the Council' in Fermanagh (Brookeborough, Derrylea and Irvinestown); Florencecourt, held by Lord Enniskillen in the 1949 return and by the Earl of Enniskillen in the 1955 return (FMH 21 May 1949 p. 3; FMH 4 June 1955 p. 8), is not among the changes, so its sitting member was returned again. The Herald's 24 May 1952 summary lists only nineteen divisions and omits this one.

note: Triennial election of Fermanagh County Council, polled Thursday 5 June 1952 (Belfast News-Letter, 6 June 1952: polling 'took place yesterday in Northern Ireland'). The only county council contest was Newtownbutler; the other eighteen divisions were uncontested and are named in the Herald list of 24 May 1952. The printed list contains nineteen divisions; Florencecourt, present in 1939, is not among them, but the News-Letter's 21 May 1952 nominations report says there were only three changes in the personnel of the Council, so its sitting member (the Earl of Enniskillen) was returned again. Structure and division names for the 1966-67 amalgamation are in notes/fermanagh-fcra-1969.md, from Fermanagh CRA, 'Fermanagh Facts' (1969). That is an advocacy pamphlet: use it for names only, not figures. Its register figures are disputed by Kingsley (2021) on the Omagh Rural District scheme. Read the page image before recording any number from it. division inferred from the 21 May 1949 return (Lord Enniskillen); the Fermanagh Herald of 2 August 1952, p. 3, names Lord Enniskillen at a meeting of the new County Council, and he is its chairman by October 1952 (Fermanagh Herald, 11 October 1952, p. 5). No co-option, by-election or other member for Florencecourt found. The News-Letter reported only three changes of personnel (Brookeborough, Derrylea, Irvinestown). Released 7 Nov 2026 (round 2). Returned unopposed.
